### § 1. Election, term, etc.; Deputy Comptroller; Staff. {#s-1}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Election and qualifications; Term; Salary; Term limit.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The voters of Baltimore City shall elect a Comptroller of the City on the Tuesday next after the first Monday in November 2016, and on the same day and month in every succeeding fourth year.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The Comptroller shall possess the same qualifications as prescribed in this Charter for the Mayor.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>The term of the Comptroller shall commence on the Tuesday next after the first Monday in December succeeding the election and shall continue for 4 years and until a successor has been elected and qualified.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>The Comptroller's salary shall be set as provided in <a href="article-vii.html">Article VII</a>, §§ <a href="article-vii.html#s-117">117</a> through <a href="article-vii.html#s-125">125</a> of this Charter.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>A Comptroller shall not hold office for more than 2 consecutive full terms of office and in no event shall hold the office for more than 8 years during any12 year period. This provision shall not preclude an elected Comptroller from seeking other elected offices within Baltimore City after two consecutive terms as Comptroller. In the event that an elected Comptroller takes office as a result of a removal or vacancy described in <a href="article-v.html#s-2">§ 2 of this Article</a>, that elected Comptroller shall only be eligible to hold that office for the remainder of the predecessor’s unexpired term and 1 consecutive full term thereafter.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Deputy; Staff.</span></p>
<p>The Comptroller shall appoint, to aid in the discharge of the Comptroller’s duties, a Deputy Comptroller and such other employees as provided in the Ordinance of Estimates.  In case of temporary absence or disqualification of the Comptroller, the Deputy Comptroller shall, during such absence or disqualification from any cause, perform the duties of the Comptroller, including the Comptroller’s duties as a member of the Board of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Initiative “Question K”, ratified Nov. 8, 2022; Res. 99-016, ratified Nov. 2, 1999; Res. 04-049, ratified Nov. 2, 2004; Res. 05-009, ratified Nov. 7, 2006; Res. 12-003, ratified Nov. 6, 2012</p>
```


### § 2. Removal; Vacancy. {#s-2}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Removal.</span></p>
<p>The City Council, by a three-fourths vote of its members, may remove the Comptroller from office for incompetency, misconduct in office, wilful neglect of duty, or felony or misdemeanor in office, on charges preferred by the Mayor, by the City Council's Committee on Legislative Investigations, a verified petition signed by at least 20% of the qualified voters in Baltimore City, or by the Inspector General, and after notice of  those charges and an opportunity to be heard by the City Council are given to the Comptroller.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Vacancy.</span></p>
<p>In the event of the death, resignation, or removal from office of the Comptroller, a successor, to fill out the unexpired term, shall be elected by the City Council by a majority vote of its members.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>Editor's Notes, History:</strong> Res. 20-024, ratified Nov. 3, 2020; Paragraph (a)(5) was added by Initiative Ballot Question K, ratified November 8, 2022.  The final sentence of Question K establishes that paragraph (a)(5) will be effective “beginning with persons elected in the 2024 Baltimore City Election.”</p>
```


### § 3. General duties. {#s-3}

```{=html}
<p>The Comptroller shall:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span></p>
<p>serve as a member of the Board of Estimates;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span></p>
<p>serve as a member of the Board of Finance;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span></p>
<p>have such general supervision of the Department of Audits and the activities of the City Auditor as provided for in the Charter;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span></p>
<p>be responsible for the proper conduct, management and operation of the Department of Real Estate; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span></p>
<p>subject to the approval of the Board of Estimates, and within the limits of the appropriation therefor in the Ordinance of Estimates, obtain such insurance as may be necessary for the proper protection of the City or as may be required by applicable law, and shall, whenever it would be to the City’s advantage, seek competitive bids for the insurance;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(f)</span></p>
<p>be responsible for the proper conduct, management and operation of the Department of Accounts Payable; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(g)</span></p>
<p>perform such other duties, not inconsistent with the office, as prescribed by law.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 22-004, ratified Nov. 8, 2022</p>
```


### § 4. Department of Real Estate – Established. {#s-4}

```{=html}
<p>There shall be a Department of Real Estate, the head of which shall be the Comptroller.</p>
<p>For the conduct of the Department, the Comptroller shall appoint a Real Estate Officer and such assistants and employees as may be provided for in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
```


### § 5. Department of Real Estate – Duties. {#s-5}

```{=html}
<p>The Department of Real Estate shall have the following responsibilities in all matters relating to the acquisition, sale, lease, exchange or other disposition of real property of the City; provided, however, that nothing in <a href="article-v.html#s-5">this section</a> shall affect the exercise by the City by ordinance of the powers granted to it in sub<a href="article-ii.html#s-15">section (15) of Article II</a>, or by the Mayor of the powers provided by <a href="article-iv.html#s-4">Section 4(c) of Article IV</a> relating to economic development:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Negotiation of acquisitions.</span></p>
<p>Subject to any limitation on this power elsewhere in the Charter, any purchase (other than by condemnation) of real property or an interest therein by the City shall (unless and to the extent otherwise provided by the Board of Estimates) be negotiated and made on its behalf by the Department of Real Estate in such a manner as the Board of Estimates shall from time to time authorize and instruct.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Disposition of City property.</span></p>
<p>The Department shall (unless and to the extent otherwise provided by the Board of Estimates) arrange for the disposition of any building or parcel of land (or any other real property) no longer needed by the City for public use.</p>
<p>Any such disposition shall be authorized by ordinance, shall be approved by the Board of Estimates with the approval entered in its minutes, and shall be made at public sale unless a private sale or other manner of disposition shall be expressly authorized by the Board of Estimates and entered in its minutes.  The instrument of conveyance of any building or parcel of land (or any other real property) whose disposition has been so authorized and approved shall be executed on behalf of the City by the Comptroller or Deputy Comptroller and attested to by the Director of Finance or the Deputy Director of Finance.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Leasing City property.</span></p>
<p>The Department is authorized to lease any building or parcel of land (or any other real property) not needed by the City for public purposes on a month to month basis, unless otherwise provided by ordinance.  It is also authorized to lease such property for fixed terms provided such leases are first approved by the Board of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Inventory of City property.</span></p>
<p>The Comptroller, working in conjunction with the heads of other affected municipal agencies, shall maintain a public inventory of the City’s properties.</p>
</div>
```


### § 6. Real Property Account. {#s-6}

```{=html}
<p>Except as may be otherwise provided by ordinance with regard to the exercise by the City of the powers granted to it in subsection (15) and sub<a href="article-ii.html#s-15a">section (15A) of Article II</a>, the Comptroller shall cause to be credited to an account to be known as the “Mayor and City Council Real Property Account”, the proceeds from the sale by the City of any real or leasehold property or interest therein.</p>
<p>Moneys received from such sales shall be appropriated in the Ordinance of Estimates only for the purchase of land, and the purchase or construction of buildings, and other construction work and projects, and to carry out the industrial and economic development powers vested in the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore by the provisions of sub<a href="article-ii.html#s-15a">section (15A) of Article II</a>, it being the intent of this provision to limit the use of such moneys to the purposes specifically mentioned in <a href="article-v.html#s-6">this section</a>, and otherwise to prohibit their use for current expenses of the City.</p>
<p>The annual Ordinance of Estimates shall include the appropriations which are proposed to be charged to the “Mayor and City Council Real Property Account”, and the state of the account, with the particulars as to sources of receipts, shall be reported by the Comptroller annually to the City Council.</p>
```


### § 7. Department of Audits – Established. {#s-7}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Establishment; City Auditor.</span></p>
<p>There shall be a Department of Audits, the head of which shall be the City Auditor.</p>
<p>The City Auditor shall be a certified public accountant who is licensed by the State of Maryland, shall be appointed by the Comptroller in accordance with the provisions of the Charter relating to the Civil Service, and shall hold office in accordance with these provisions.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Staff; Budget.</span></p>
<p>The City Auditor shall appoint such employees as may be provided in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
<p>Sufficient funds shall be included in the Ordinance of Estimates for the Department of Audits to enable the City Auditor to perform the duties prescribed herein.</p>
</div>
```


### § 8. Department of Audits – General powers and duties. {#s-8}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">In general.</span></p>
<p>In accordance with generally accepted government auditing standards and State and federal law, the City Auditor:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>shall at appropriate intervals conduct an audit of the financial transactions of every municipal agency, except the Department of Audits;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>shall conduct an annual audit of all accounts, revenues, and receipts of the City;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>shall conduct biennial audits of principal agencies, as provided in <a href="article-v.html#s-11">§ 11 of this article</a>;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>may audit the expenditure of City-granted funds by any public or private agency that receives such funds;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>may audit City contracts, grants, subgrants and other agreements as required by the terms and conditions of these instruments and, when the contracts, grants, subgrants and other agreements require that audits be conducted by other auditors, review such audits; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(6)</span></p>
<p>shall make such other audits as the Comptroller or the Board of Estimates may request, provided that those requested audits do not, in the judgment of the City Auditor, unduly hinder the performance of regular audits.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Subpoena.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>To perform the duties of his or her office, the City Auditor may issue a subpoena to any municipal officer, municipal employee, or any other person receiving City funds to require the production of any information, document, report, record, account, or other material.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The City Auditor may enforce any subpoena issued pursuant to this subsection in any court of competent jurisdiction.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Reports.</span></p>
<p>The City Auditor shall make reports of all such audits to the Comptroller and, at the same time, to each of the other members of the Board of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 16-031, ratified Nov. 8, 2016; Res. 20-022, ratified Nov. 3, 2020</p>
```


### § 9. Department of Audits – Comprehensive annual financial report. {#s-9}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Audit of report.</span></p>
<p>The City Auditor, under the supervision of the Comptroller, shall audit the comprehensive annual financial report of the City, prepared by the Director of Finance.  This report shall be a public document.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Access to records.</span></p>
<p>To carry out the Auditor’s duties, the Auditor shall have access at all times to the financial records of all municipal agencies and the relevant financial records of contractors with, and grantees of, the City.</p>
</div>
```


### § 10. Department of Audits – Independent auditors. {#s-10}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Required engagement.</span></p>
<p>The Board of Estimates, at appropriate intervals, shall engage an independent firm of certified public accountants to audit:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>the financial transactions of the Department of Audits; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>the comprehensive annual financial report of the City.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Permissive engagement.</span></p>
<p>The Board of Estimates may engage an independent firm of certified public accountants to audit the financial transactions of any municipal agency and to examine the fiscal procedures, records, accounts, and methods of any municipal agency, including the Department of Audits.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Reports.</span></p>
<p>The independent firm of certified public accountants shall make reports of its audits, examinations, and recommendations to the Board of Estimates.</p>
</div>
```


### § 11. Department of Audits – Biennial audits of principal agencies. {#s-11}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Definitions.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">In general.</span></p>
<p>In <a href="article-v.html#s-11">this section</a>, the following terms have the meanings indicated.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Audit.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>“Audit” means an audit undertaken in accordance with generally accepted government auditing standards and federal and state law.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>“Audit” includes both:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">(A)</span></p>
<p>a financial audit of a principal agency’s financial transactions, including all revenues and receipts; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">(B)</span></p>
<p>a performance audit that assesses a principal agency’s practices to determine whether the agency is operating economically and efficiently and whether corrective actions for improving its performance are appropriate.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Principal agency.</span></p>
<p>“Principal agency” means any of the following executive departments:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>
              Group A –
            </p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">1.</span></p>
<p>Department of Finance.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">2.</span></p>
<p>Department of Public Works.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">3.</span></p>
<p>Fire Department.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">4.</span></p>
<p>Department of Housing and Community Development.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">5.</span></p>
<p>Department of General Services.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">6.</span></p>
<p>Baltimore Development Corporation.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">7.</span></p>
<p>Mayor’s Office of Information Technology (or successor entity to this Office).</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">8.</span></p>
<p>Mayor’s Office of Human Services (or successor entity to this Office).</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>
              Group B –
            </p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">1.</span></p>
<p>Department of Law.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">2.</span></p>
<p>Department of Human Resources.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">3.</span></p>
<p>Department of Transportation.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">4.</span></p>
<p>Police Department.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">5.</span></p>
<p>Department of Recreation and Parks.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">6.</span></p>
<p>Department of Planning.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">7.</span></p>
<p>Department of Health.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">8.</span></p>
<p>Mayor’s Office of Employment Development (or successor entity to this Office).</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Biennial audit required.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">In general.</span></p>
<p>At least twice during every 4-year term of the Mayor and City Council, the City Auditor shall conduct an audit of each principal agency’s operations for the preceding 2 fiscal years.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Staggered schedule.</span></p>
<p>These audits shall be staggered so that:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>audits of the principal agencies listed in subsection (a)(3)(i) as “Group A” are initiated in odd-numbered calendar years; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>audits of the principal agencies listed in subsection (a)(3)(ii) as “Group B” are initiated in even-numbered calendar years.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Costs of audit.</span></p>
<p>In each fiscal year preceding the fiscal year in which audits are to be conducted under <a href="article-v.html#s-11">this section</a>, the Comptroller shall include the costs of those audits in the estimates that the Comptroller submits for the next year’s Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Status of prior recommendations.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">In general.</span></p>
<p>Each report of an agency audit conducted under <a href="article-v.html#s-11">this section</a> shall include an ancillary report on the status of all recommendations for executive action that resulted from that agency’s immediately preceding audit under <a href="article-v.html#s-11">this section</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Content of report.</span></p>
<p>The ancillary report shall:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>designate each recommendation’s status either as “implemented”, “partially implemented”, or “not implemented”; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>provide justification for the status designation assigned.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Publication of reports.</span></p>
<p>Reports of all audits conducted under <a href="article-v.html#s-11">this section</a> shall be:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>posted on a public website maintained by the City Comptroller;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>filed with the Department of Legislative Reference;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>submitted to the principal agency audited; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>submitted to each member of:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>the Board of Estimates;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>the City Council; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>the Biennial Audits Oversight Commission.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(f)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Biennial Audits Oversight Commission.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Commission established.</span></p>
<p>There is a Biennial Audits Oversight Commission.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Composition.</span></p>
<p>The Commission comprises the following 7 members:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>the Director of Finance;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>the Inspector General;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>the Comptroller;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iv)</span></p>
<p>the City Council President; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(v)</span></p>
<p>3 members of the City Council, appointed by the City Council President.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Officers.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>The City Council President shall designate 1 of the members to serve as Chair of the Commission.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>The members of the Commission, by majority vote, may elect any other officers that they consider necessary or appropriate.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Meetings; voting.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>The Commission shall meet at the call of the Chair as frequently as required to perform its duties.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>4 members of the Commission constitute a quorum for the transaction of business.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>An affirmative vote of at least 4 members is needed for any official action.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Procedures.</span></p>
<p>The Commission may adopt rules of procedure to govern its meetings and operations.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(6)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Powers and duties.</span></p>
<p>The Commission:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>shall provide guidance and advice to the City Auditor in determining the scope of a principal agency’s performance audit;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>shall hold at least 2 publicly advertised meetings a year, at which meetings the City Auditor shall appear and report on the status of the audits and recommendations under <a href="article-v.html#s-11">this section</a>; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>for good cause shown by a principal agency, may waive the requirement for a financial audit to be conducted under <a href="article-v.html#s-11">this section</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>Editor's Notes, History:</strong> Res. 16-031, ratified Nov. 8, 2016; Res. 20-022, ratified Nov. 3, 2020; For statutory requirements governing the proposal, adoption, and publication of administrative rules and regulations, see General Provisions Article, Title 4 {“Administrative Procedure Act – Regulations”}.</p>
```


### § 12. Department of Accounts Payable– Established. {#s-12}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">In general.</span></p>
<p>There shall be a Department of Accounts Payable, the head of which shall be the Director of the Department, who shall be appointed by the Comptroller.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Staff.</span></p>
<p>The Director shall appoint such employees as may be provided in the Ordinance of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 22-004, ratified Nov. 8, 2022</p>
```


### § 13. Department of Accounts Payable – General powers and duties. {#s-13}

```{=html}
<p>Except as otherwise provided in <a href="article-vii.html#s-10">Article VII, § 10</a> {“Department of Finance: Disbursements related to salary or compensation.”}:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>the Department of Accounts Payable shall have general supervision and charge over all payments and disbursements made by the City; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>no payment or disbursement may be made by the City without the approval of the Department.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 22-004, ratified Nov. 8, 2022</p>
```


### § 14. Department of Accounts Payable – Withdrawals; Signatures for checks. {#s-14}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Withdrawals.</span></p>
<p>The Director shall approve the withdrawal of City moneys from their depositories.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Required signatures for checks.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">In general.</span></p>
<p>Except as provided for in <a href="article-vii.html#s-12">Article VII, § 12</a> {“Department of Finance: Collections, deposits, withdrawals, etc.”}, and unless otherwise provided by law, all checks of the City issued by or for the Department of Accounts Payable shall be signed by the Comptroller or Director and counter-signed by the Mayor.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Form of signature.</span></p>
<p>Any signature on checks of the City may be manual or facsimile.</p>
</div>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 22-004, ratified Nov. 8, 2022</p>
```


### § 15. Department of Accounts Payable – Reporting. {#s-15}

```{=html}
<p>The Comptroller and the Director of the Department shall deliver all information related to the operation of the Department to the Director of the Department of Finance, at the frequency and in the format required by the Director of Finance, to enable the Director of Finance to perform his or her duties as provided for in <a href="article-vii.html">Article VII</a>.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Res. 22-004, ratified Nov. 8, 2022</p>
```
